To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

short-term administration of anti-ICAM/LFA-1/LFA1 or anti-CD8 during a critical period at younger age results in complete protection of murine autoimmune diabetes, and that tolerance mechanisms like anergy, clonal deletion, immunoregulation or Th1 toTh2/Th3 shifting do not play any role in the protection.
the short-term administration of anti-ICAM/LFA-1 and anti-CD 8 mAbs during a critical period in young NOD mice induces a complete protection against diabetes.
tolerance mechanisms in murine diabetes induced by anti-LFA-1/ICAM-1 and anti-CD 8 mAb were not responsible for the protection from diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms responsible for the tolerance induced by short-term treatment of antibodies against ICAMA-1/LFA1 and CD8 molecules during the critical period of younger NOD mice.
the mechanisms of tolerance induction in murine autoimmune type 1 diabetes.
the development of new therapeutic approaches to prevent the progression of autoimmune diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tolerance mechanism in this system is a combination of several factors.
the tolerance mechanism in autoimmune diabetes induced by mAb is still unknown.

tolerance mechanisms induced by the administration of anti-ICAM/LFA-1 and CD8 mAb during the critical period of young age in NOD mice is due to a loss of the ability of autoreactive CD8+ T cells to enter into islets, which is probably due to a loss or down-regulation of adhesion molecules on the surface of CD8+ T lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
tolerance induction is a complex process and may be achieved by different mechanisms depending on the nature of the antigen and/or the age of the animal.
anti-ICAM/LFA-1 and anti-CD-8 mAbs induced a state of tolerance in NOD mice, which is characterized by the loss of capability for T cells to infiltrating and destroying pancreatic beta-cells.
anti-ICAM1/LFA- 1 or anti-CD8 treatment of NOD mice during younger age could protect them from autoimmune diabetes, but the tolerance mechanisms involved are not clear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of protection is not clonal deletion, energy, or regulatory cells.
we can use the anti-ICAM-LFA1 antibody to treat autoimmune diabetes in Nod mice.
we have identified a mechanism that prevents autoimmune diabetes in mice.
